# Intentional exceptions to the fingerprint scan, one literal substring per line.
# Matched literally by `grep -F`, so they are exact strings, not regexes.
#
# WHY THIS FILE EXISTS
#
# The scan in .github/workflows/ci.yml is deliberately narrow, and this file
# is where a reviewed-and-accepted exception would be written down. It is
# currently EMPTY, which means the scan has no exceptions at all.
#
# That is the correct state, and it is deliberately not the same as deleting
# the file: an allowlist that can be emptied without anyone noticing is not an
# allowlist. Keeping the mechanism, visibly empty, is the record.
#
# Adding a line here is a decision to publish that string. Do not add one to
# make a red build go green without asking why it was red.
#
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------
# WHAT USED TO BE HERE
#
# One entry: the repository owner's own work address (value withheld here).
#
# It was found during the pre-publication scrub and offered for removal. The
# owner chose to keep it, on the grounds that correct attribution of their own
# work is worth more than the address not appearing. That was a defensible
# call, and it was implemented rather than argued with: the address was
# allowlisted, the reasoning was recorded, and the reversal was documented so
# it stayed a choice instead of drifting into an accident.
#
# The repository was private throughout, which is what made keeping it
# reasonable. Publishing changed the arithmetic. A live work mailbox becomes
# world-readable and harvestable the moment a repository is public, and it
# cannot be un-published -- GitHub does not offer a scrub for a public
# repository's history, so the exposure is permanent and the only fix is
# rewriting and re-publishing, which is exactly the expensive thing to do
# afterwards. The commits would also have rendered from an unverified
# contributor, since the address is not verified on the account.
#
# So the decision was reversed while the repository was still private, and the
# cost was one filter-repo pass instead of a support request. All eight
# commits are now authored and committed by Abaabeel, at
# Abaabeel@users.noreply.github.com -- an address GitHub verifies, which
# preserves attribution without exposing a mailbox. The commits now show as
# verified contributions.
#
# The guard pattern in ci.yml still lists the old address as a fingerprint to
# reject, on purpose. It is no longer an exception that needs allowing; it is
# now a string that must not come back. An empty allowlist plus a pattern that
# still names the string is the configuration that makes the reversal
# enforceable rather than merely recorded.
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------
